description: Run the native `/pan-exec-waves 1` workflow on the seeded two-plan phase and check the chain produced what the protocol promises: a summary per plan, a verification for the phase, and the seed's functions actually built.
why: Plan item 5c — the behavioural gate §3.2 asked for. The static gate proves the script parses and names the right agents; only a run shows whether the wave dispatch completes without dropping a step, which is the exact defect class PanLoop finding 0 measured in the markdown path (0/3 → 16/16). Compare against markdown-exec-phase-chain on the same seed; run both --repeat 5 before believing either number. Measurement note (2026-09-10): the first two runs of this scenario died at ~605 s with `Workflow aborted` — headless `claude -p` abandons a background Workflow after ten minutes by default (CLAUDE_CODE_PRINT_BG_WAIT_CEILING_MS). The runner now lifts that ceiling; results from before this note measured the ceiling, not the chain.

steps.why: The seed must index as two waves with no checkpoints — otherwise the script refuses by design and the run measures the seed, not the workflow.

The four observable outcomes of a complete chain: both summaries (the executors finished), the code (the plans were really executed, not summarised), and a verification file (the Verify phase ran). A missing 01-02 summary with 01-01 present is the boundary-drop signature.
The seed's own `npm test` passes in the workspace — the executors built working code, not files that look right.
